## Cause

Commit `4d99828` ("Drop indexes with no recorded reads — Q3 storage review") dropped `ux_payment_idempotency_key`:

`src/main/resources/db/migration/V3__drop_unused_indexes.sql:6`
```sql
DROP INDEX IF EXISTS ux_payment_idempotency_key;
```

That index was added by `V2__payment_unique_index.sql` as the database half of the idempotency fix. The storage review's premise was wrong: a unique index backing a constraint is enforced on *write*, so it never accumulates reads in `pg_stat_user_indexes`. Zero reads meant "constraint", not "unused".

`PaymentService.create` (`src/main/java/mn/payments/PaymentService.java:29`) still does its `existsByIdempotencyKey` check inside the transaction, but that check only serializes within one node. Two concurrent requests with the same key on different cluster nodes both read `false` and both insert — the index was the only thing making the database the final arbiter. Dropping it reopened exactly the race `5940039` closed.

## Fix

**`V4__restore_payment_unique_index.sql`** (new) recreates the index, with a comment explaining why it looks unused so the next storage review doesn't drop it again. I did not edit `V3` — it has already run in production and Flyway checksums it.

The migration first raises a readable error if any duplicate `idempotency_key` rows exist. **This is likely to fire on your production deploy**: the rows written while the index was missing are the double charges, and `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX` cannot succeed until they're reconciled. Deciding which duplicate survives and which gets refunded is a money decision, so the migration refuses rather than deleting rows itself. Find them with:

```sql
SELECT idempotency_key, count(*) FROM payment GROUP BY 1 HAVING count(*) > 1;
```

I also updated two comments in `Payment.java` and `PaymentService.java` that pointed at `V2` as the source of the index.

Two things I left alone, flagging rather than changing:

- `V3` also dropped `ix_payment_status_created`. That one is a genuine lookup path, so the "no reads" finding may have been legitimate — it's a performance question, unrelated to double-charging, and I didn't want to bundle it into a correctness fix.
- `PaymentService.create` builds the new `Payment` setting only `status` — `id`, `idempotencyKey`, and `amount` are never set, and `Payment` has no setters for them. This predates the regression (the pre-`5940039` `insert()` had the same shape), so it isn't what changed in production, but as written the insert can't satisfy the `NOT NULL` columns and the unique index has no key to enforce on. Worth a look separately.

I haven't run the build — there's no DB or Flyway configuration in the repo to migrate against.
